bases.manual: no honest mechanical check reaches this practice; a human answers the stated question
bases.not-applicable: the practice does not apply here, for the stated standing reason
bases.recorded: the practice is discharged by a system outside this tree; the in-tree record of it is the evidence
bases.verified-in-tree: the evidence artefact itself stands in this tree and was examined by the checker

practices.evidence_rule: raw/ exists holding at least 100 files, and evaluation/citation-lockfile.json exists and locks at least 1 raw source by hash.
practices.paper: Data management: save the data as originally obtained
practices.statement: Raw material is kept exactly as it arrived, in its own layer, apart from everything derived from it — and held under change detection, so a silent edit would show.

practices.evidence_rule: git reports at least one remote, evaluation/checkpoints.jsonl carries at least one checkpoint, and the witness directory ~/workspace/wiki-checkpoints exists outside the repo.
practices.paper: Data management: back up the data
practices.statement: Everything is backed up off the machine that holds it: a canonical remote home for the tree, plus signed checkpoints witnessed outside the repository.

practices.evidence_rule: At least half of the compiled pages (wiki/**/*.md except index/log) carry a filled compiled_date stamp. Below that, the steps live only in central logs — recorded, but not on the artefact.
practices.paper: Data management: record all the steps used to process data
practices.statement: The steps that turn raw material into a derived page are recorded on the page itself (its compile stamp), so any derivation can be repeated and audited.

practices.evidence_rule: evaluation/claim-index.jsonl, evaluation/tag-registry.jsonl and evaluation/decisions-register.jsonl each exist and are non-empty.
practices.paper: Data management: use unique identifiers for data and references
practices.statement: Anything that must be referred to again — claims, tags, decisions, checkpoints — carries a unique, persistent identifier in a register.

practices.evidence_rule: Standing reason: this is a private personal wiki by the owner's decision; its canonical home is a private Azure repository and nothing in it is published as a dataset. The practice falls due again the day any part of the wiki is published as data.
practices.paper: Data management: submit data to a reputable repository / assign a DOI
practices.statement: Data is deposited in a public repository under a persistent identifier (a DOI).

practices.evidence_rule: At least 95% of scripts/*.py carry a module docstring (parsed, not grepped).
practices.paper: Software: place a brief explanatory comment at the start of every program
practices.statement: Every program opens with a brief statement of what it does, before any code.

practices.evidence_rule: A licence file stands at the tree root (LICENSE, LICENCE, COPYING, or a capitalisation variant).
practices.paper: Software: make the software citable and licensed for reuse
practices.statement: The work carries an explicit licence, so anyone who holds a copy knows what they may do with it.

practices.evidence_rule: scripts/tests/ exists and holds at least 50 test files.
practices.paper: Software: test libraries and programs before relying on them
practices.statement: The software is tested, and the test suite is part of the project — not an afterthought kept elsewhere.

practices.evidence_rule: Question for a human: pick any three scripts at random — is each one job, are its functions named for what they return or do, and does any block of logic appear twice in the tree where one shared copy would do?
practices.paper: Software: decompose programs into functions; be ruthless about eliminating duplication; use meaningful names
practices.statement: Programs are decomposed into small, named, single-job pieces; duplication is removed rather than copied; names say what things are.

practices.evidence_rule: Question for a human: for the last three tools built, does a build note or research record show the prior-art search (the wiki's research protocol requires SIFT + source opening) — or was each built from a blank page?
practices.paper: Software: always search for well-maintained software libraries that do what you need
practices.statement: Before building something new, the landscape is searched for a well-maintained existing answer, and what is found is recorded.

practices.evidence_rule: README.md exists at the root and wiki/overview.md exists.
practices.paper: Collaboration: create a project overview / make it easy for others to join
practices.statement: A newcomer can start from a written overview: a README that says what this is and how it is organised, and a living synthesis of the whole.

practices.evidence_rule: git reports the canonical remote (azure) for this tree, so every admitted collaborator reads and files against the same HEAD.
practices.paper: Collaboration: work in a shared, public directory; make changes visible
practices.statement: Work happens in one shared, canonical place that every collaborator can see — not in private copies that drift apart.

practices.evidence_rule: raw/filings/ holds filings from at least two distinct admitted agents — the channel through which critique of this wiki has actually arrived.
practices.paper: Collaboration: comment and critique one another's work
practices.statement: Collaborators examine and critique one another's work, and the critiques are kept on the record.

practices.evidence_rule: The directories raw/, wiki/, scripts/, evaluation/, templates/ and tools/ all exist.
practices.paper: Project organization: put each project in its own directory, with a standard layout
practices.statement: Each kind of material has one stated home, and the layout is standard enough to be guessed: raw, wiki, scripts, evaluation, templates, tools.

practices.evidence_rule: Zero basenames with spaces or uppercase letters among wiki/**/*.md and scripts/*.py (raw material keeps the names it arrived with and is out of scope).
practices.paper: Project organization: name files and folders meaningfully and consistently
practices.statement: Files we name are named for their content in the house style: lowercase, hyphenated, no spaces.

practices.evidence_rule: Every regular file at the root is on the standing list (AGENTS.md, README.md, Home.md, purpose.md, CONVERSATION-LOG.md, owner-rights-reversal-notice.md, azure-pipelines.yml, .gitignore, .gitattributes, and a root licence file when one stands). Anything else is named as a violation.
practices.paper: Project organization: keep the project directory tidy and navigable
practices.statement: The project root holds only the project's named standing documents and its folders; working scraps and one-off prompts live in their own places.

practices.evidence_rule: A .git directory exists with at least 100 commits and at least 1,000 tracked files.
practices.paper: Tracking changes: use version control; back up (almost) everything created
practices.statement: Everything created is under version control, and the history is kept — not squashed away.

practices.evidence_rule: wiki/log.md exists and its newest dated entry is no more than 14 days older than the run date.
practices.paper: Tracking changes: use a changelog
practices.statement: A changelog records what was done, entry by entry with dates, as it happens — not reconstructed later.

practices.evidence_rule: evaluation/checkpoints.jsonl is non-empty and evaluation/checkpoints.d/ holds at least one signed checkpoint record.
practices.paper: Tracking changes: use version numbers / version everything
practices.statement: States of the work are versioned and witnessed, so any earlier state can be named, recovered and checked.

practices.evidence_rule: At least 99% of files under wiki/ are plain text (.md, .json, .jsonl, .txt, .yaml, .yml, .csv, extension-less text, .gitkeep).
practices.paper: Manuscripts: write in plain-text formats under version control
practices.statement: Records are kept in durable, open, plain-text formats that any future reader can open without the tools that wrote them.

practices.evidence_rule: evaluation/decisions-register.jsonl exists and is non-empty, and at least one compiled decisions page stands in wiki/syntheses/.
practices.paper: Manuscripts: keep the record of the work with the work
practices.statement: Decisions are recorded where a future reader will find them — in a register and on pages — never left only in a chat thread.

practices.evidence_rule: Question for a human: for the last three deliverables, was the reader named before writing, and was the form chosen for that reader (for this wiki's owner: a finished PDF, not a raw markdown file)?
practices.paper: Manuscripts: identify the audience and write for it
practices.statement: Every document is written for a named reader, in the form that reader can actually use.

source: Restated in our own words from the Box 1 recommendations of Wilson et al., "Good Enough Practices in Scientific Computing", PLOS Computational Biology 13(6): e1005510 (2017), CC-BY 4.0. No text is copied; each practice is re-worded for a personal LLM wiki and paired with the local evidence that would show it is actually done.
title: Good-enough practices — the floor this wiki holds itself to
